design_changes: 4.1: a same-runtime segment gets a session of its own (setsid on MSYS2, perl POSIX::setsid on Git for Windows - no setsid there): its --session self stray checks must never see the caller's other detached processes (the ktests runner's sibling test files when 050-052 run a gate, an agent's jobs)
4.1: PATH crosses via the environment (cygwin converts it), not via the spec; the spec carries LANG/LC_*/TZ/COMSPEC/SYSTEMROOT/WINDIR/...

4.1: the per-cell timeout is the watchdog's third request (seg-N.cur 'run IDX DEADLINE'): no timeout binary, no fork; requests = reason in seg-N.why + USR1 repeated every tick until seg-N.ack holds the same reason; a late timeout USR1 of the previous cell is acked and the wait resumed
4.1: segment-killed stops by session (kt_strays_stop --session self --since SEGMENT_START: TERM at each tree root, ktests.sh stops its group, KILL after), no pgid needed

4.1 measured: a tree kill of the LAUNCHER does not reach the segment (env/setsid exec chain cuts the Windows parent link), in every direction; the segment stops on the stale heartbeat. The watchdog's own path is exercised by a tree kill of the SEGMENT (its winpid in seg-N.pid)

4.1: lines: segment appends seg-N.lines, the launcher is the single writer of stdout/progress.txt (1 s relay); the cross-runtime stub runs in a process group of its own (set -m) so a terminal Ctrl-C reaches the launcher only

4.2: deny-by-default env (env -i start + unset all exported vars but PATH/PWD/SHLVL + all exported functions, fork-free; export only the whitelist from the spec); OLDPWD unset per cell; MSYSTEM=MINGW64 is added by both runtimes to every process started without it (cannot be removed, not the caller's)

4.3: CRASH also for summary 'error REASON' and for a missing summary after rc 0; INTERRUPTED for cells the gate stopped (counted apart); a stray found only by the final check turns its cell STRAY afterwards; __GATE__ fail field = FAIL + CRASH
launcher: a segment killed from outside while the launcher lives -> [WARN], FAIL, rc 1; a lost parent -> 143
G2.nohup: implemented: --nohup turns the parent watch off, and so does nohup (SIGHUP ignored on entry). Reason: the watch cannot tell a parent killed at the Windows level from one that exited normally (both kill -0 failures); a run detached on purpose loses its parent by design and would stop itself at once. run_in_background keeps the parent alive: no flag needed

design_decisions: cell order inside a runtime: repeat > suite > mode > cwd; SUITE#R in the line when --repeat > 1

FLAKY keeps the full run's total/passed/failed and [FAIL] lines (no merged counts: the summary has no per-file counts); rerun files in cells/NNN/rerun-R/; a rerun leaving a process -> STRAY; no ENV retry inside reruns; -n appended after ARGS (the runner takes the last -n); numbers passed without leading zeros

SKIPPED is its own verdict (not NOTRUN), counted apart, in no __GATE__ field; OUT/FAILFAST read by every segment before each cell (works for --parallel too); serially the launcher writes SKIPPED results for a runtime it does not start
